The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

CME’s bitcoin cash, uniswap futures, global PMIs: Crypto Week Ahead. Your look at what's coming in the week starting Oct. 19. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin whale moves $34 million in BTC it got in 2013 when coins traded at $131. A bitcoin wallet dormant since 2013 moved 411 BTC, now worth about $34 million. It is one of several long-dormant wallets to wake up recently. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Zcash developers plan a fix to keep ZEC swaps private from future quantum computers. The team behind Zakura wants every swap through NEAR Intents to get its own key, so a refund address left on NEAR’s public chain can’t expose a user’s wider payment history. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

XRP Ledger is set to fix its lending code before anyone can use it. Validators have a bug-fix patch on course to go live Friday. The lending system it partly repairs is still 10 votes short of approval. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin, Korea’s Kospi and Nasdaq futures rally as China GDP beats estimates. Bitcoin, Nasdaq futures and Asian stocks rally as stronger-than-expected China GDP and falling oil prices lift risk appetite. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Deutsche Bank targets Asia crypto custody expansion in 2027 as German launch nears. The service will initially support bitcoin, ether and the stablecoins USDC, EURC and EURAU, with the bank managing clients’ wallets and private keys. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $82,704 with a +1.02% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,432.87 with a +0.65% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Cryptocurrency regulation: U.S. laws and global developments
items.description: Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it's an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress established a federal framework for stablecoins. Broader regulation of digital asset markets remains unsettled, although Congress and federal regulators have taken steps toward clarifying which assets and activities fall under securities or commodities

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’s Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On April 1, 2026, the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the GENIUS Act), a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

# Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

Coin Gabbar

Coin Gabbar@coin\_gabbar\_·

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
